subject: Procurement intake: vendor setup & payment terms
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement intake: vendor setup & payment terms for Redwood

Hi Dylan —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks from Acme procurement so we can move to vendor setup: 

- Can you share your vendor setup packet (vendor contact, tax docs, sample invoice)?
- We need a completed W-9 on file for payments (or W-8 if non-US).
- What payment methods do you accept: PO (net terms) vs. corporate card? Which do you prefer for enterprise deals?
- Are you listed on AWS Marketplace or any other marketplace? If so, can PO flow through that marketplace?
- Do you have a standard MSA / Master Services Agreement we should review?

If possible we’d like to receive the packet and W-9 this week so we can open the vendor record and set up ACH/terms. Invoice recipient will be acctspayable@acme-analytics.com.

Thanks — Sophie Lang
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics

P.S. Please include a contact for vendor portal registration and any vendor portal URLs if you use one.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement intake: vendor setup & payment terms for Redwood

Thanks Sophie — good talking earlier. Attaching the packet and our most recent W-9 for your procurement team. Quick answers inline below: 

On Mon, Aug 2, 2026 at 2:10 PM Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
> - Can you share your vendor setup packet (vendor contact, tax docs, sample invoice)?
> - We need a completed W-9 on file for payments (or W-8 if non-US).
> - What payment methods do you accept: PO (net terms) vs. corporate card? Which do you prefer for enterprise deals?
> - Are you listed on AWS Marketplace or any other marketplace? If so, can PO flow through that marketplace?
> - Do you have a standard MSA / Master Services Agreement we should review?

Responses:
- Vendor packet attached: Redwood_Vendor_Packet.pdf (contains contact, remit details, sample invoice).
- W-9 attached: Redwood_W9.pdf. If you later need a W-8, let us know and we’ll provide the correct form.
- Payment methods: we accept both PO (preferred for enterprise) and corporate card. Standard commercial terms are net-30; we can consider net-45 for larger, contracted deals with an executed SOW or amendment.
- Marketplace: Redwood is available on select marketplaces. For this account we typically onboard as a direct vendor to simplify contract and SLAs; we can discuss marketplace procurement if that’s your preference — PO routing through a marketplace depends on the marketplace’s billing flow.
- MSA: we have a standard MSA we use for customers. If you’d like, I can have Marissa loop in and send the most recent MSA and a vendor intake form for completion.

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll attach the vendor packet and W-9 (done).
2) Marissa will send the MSA + vendor intake form and raise a DocuSign envelope for signature.
3) Once the intake form + W-9 and signed MSA are in, we’ll push the vendor into our portal and share the secure banking details flow for ACH.

Attachments: Redwood_Vendor_Packet.pdf, Redwood_W9.pdf

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0182

Thanks Dylan — received the attachments and forwarding to our AP team. A couple follow-ups from AP/procurement: 

- Our AP prefers net-30 but will accept net-45 for contracted/enterprise deals. Can you confirm whether Redwood will agree to net-45 in writing or only by exception?
- Invoices should be sent to acctspayable@acme-analytics.com; do you require a specific PO format or minimum info on the invoice?
- If we onboard via a marketplace, can we still get the SLA/uptime commitments in the contract or does the marketplace biller limit that?
- For banking: we’ll need your vendor portal registration and where to enter bank details securely; can you provide the portal URL or the person who sends the invite?

If Marissa can send the MSA + intake form and confirm the portal flow, we’ll aim to complete by the end of the week.

Best — Sophie

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acme-analytics.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 15:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement intake: vendor setup & payment terms for Redwood

Hi Sophie — looping in to handle the vendor paperwork. Thanks for the detailed questions.

Answers and immediate next steps:
- Net terms: standard is net-30 (written in our invoice terms). We can agree net-45 by exception for larger, signed deals; that would be documented in the MSA or an amendment (we’re happy to include that language if you confirm it’s needed).
- Invoice requirements: please include your PO number, account name, remit address, and the line-level PO if applicable. Our sample invoice in the vendor packet shows required fields.
- Marketplace vs direct: marketplace billing sometimes constrains contract language. For guaranteed SLA language and custom terms we recommend direct vendor onboarding + MSA. If you still want marketplace, we’ll coordinate to map the SLA into the marketplace ordering terms where possible.
- Banking / vendor portal: we do not send bank details over email. After you complete the attached Vendor_Intake_Form.docx we will create a vendor record and send a secure vendor-portal invite (from vendor-portal@redwood.com) where you can upload bank info for ACH. If you prefer a remit-only form for credit card payments, note that as well on the intake form.

I’ve attached the current MSA (Redwood_MSA_v2.pdf) and the Vendor_Intake_Form.docx. I will open a DocuSign envelope for the MSA and the vendor intake packet today and follow up with the portal invite once the intake form + W-9 are received.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v2.pdf, Vendor_Intake_Form.docx

Let me know if you’d like a quick 15-minute sync with procurement to walk through the intake form — happy to schedule.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Procurement Operations, Redwood Inference
